question: Is the DAG runner's per-node cpu_timeout verdict load-immune? I.e. when host load rises ~10x, does the kill-decision variable (per-cgroup accrued CPU-seconds) stay put so a burner is still caught and healthy nodes are not false-killed?
runner: agent-utils checkout 1c7c855 (parent gitlink), python engine (SAFE_CI_DAG_RUNNER_ENGINE=python); enforces per-step cpu_timeout via 1 Hz cpu.stat usage_usec poll + whole-cgroup reap (#7 / 0eb4203, landed both engines)
boxing: systemd --user transient scope; per-step child cgroups; cpu.stat usage_usec attributed per-step (sibling-independent, CPUQuota not cpuset -> co-tenant CPU cannot inflate a step's own usage_usec)
dag: probe.json (3 nodes): cpu_breach (busy-loop, cpu_timeout=2), compliant_idle (sleep 4, cpu_timeout=2), compliant_cpu (~1 CPU-s then exit, cpu_timeout=5)

legs.idle: no injected load; box executing ~5% (13/316 cores), load1 42.6
legs.busy: 128 self-owned busy-loop workers in one process group (PGID 2130415, killed by negative PGID after the run); box executing ~48% (152/316 cores), load1 62.5. Kept under the ci-hub 50% SUITABLE policy (>=160 cores left free) to remain a good co-tenant.

load_generator_disposition: self-owned PGID 2130415 confirmed killed; load returned to 4.2% executing; PGID empty verified
limitation: ~160 cores stayed free even in the busy leg, so the probe's OWN wall was not core-starved (cpu_breach wall 3.02->3.03s). This A/B therefore proves CPU-accounting sibling-independence (host load +10x, per-node usage_usec flat, verdict unchanged), NOT wall-inflation-under-scarcity. The all-wall/no-cpu limiting case (a healthy blocking wait surviving a tight CPU budget) is covered by compliant_idle here and in cpu-timeout-enforcement-verified_20260803. Deliberately did not saturate all 316 cores on a shared 18-agent box.
